PC141 course rules:
- Work must be completed individually, with groups only sharing raw data. [1]
- Examples of plagiarism include identical or nearly identical wording in reports, and copying lists, derivations, or calculations from another student. [1]
- Consequences of plagiarism include a grade of zero on the affected lab and referral to the course instructor and the University’s Academic Integrity process. [1]
- To avoid plagiarism, students should write in their own words and from their own understanding. [1]
- In tutorials, all submitted reports must represent the student's own independent work, and copying or reproducing another student's work constitutes academic dishonesty. [2]
- Any form of cheating in tutorials will be handled in accordance with the University’s Academic Integrity Policy and may result in disciplinary action. [2]

Laurier university-wide:
- Academic dishonesty includes plagiarism, which is the unacknowledged presentation of the work of others as one's own. [6]
- Plagiarism involves using the thoughts, ideas, or writings of another person and passing them off as one's own. [7] (unverified)
- Self-plagiarism is submitting the same piece of work for more than one course without the instructor’s permission. [8]

- The final grade appeal process addresses concerns regarding the application of grading criteria to the work submitted, and/or the calculation of grades only. [6][7]

- A student may submit only one (1) grade appeal per course section. [6][7]
- The chair will determine, based on the request, whether all or individual components of coursework will be re-evaluated. [8]
- The chair’s decision, whether it results in a higher grade, lower grade, or no change, will stand as the final grade. [8]

[8]

- If you will miss (or have missed) a lab session, email the instructor as soon as possible, preferably before the scheduled session. [1]
- All follow-up regarding missed labs will be handled in person during your next lab or tutorial session. [1]
- Valid reasons for absence and required documentation include: Illness, Varsity athletics travel, and Other circumstances. [1]
- Approved make-up labs must be arranged within one week, subject to section capacity and laboratory safety constraints. [1]
- Unexcused absences will result in a grade of zero for the missed laboratory. [1]

- Instructors can set clear attendance requirements and the impacts of failing to meet the attendance requirements in their syllabus for any or all of their course components. [6]

PC141 course rules:
- Work must be completed individually, with groups only sharing raw data. [1]
- Examples of plagiarism include identical or nearly identical wording in reports, and copying lists, derivations, or calculations from another student. [1]
- Consequences of plagiarism include a grade of zero on the affected lab and referral to the course instructor and the University's Academic Integrity process. [1]
- To avoid plagiarism, students should write in their own words and from their own understanding. [1]

Laurier university-wide:
- Plagiarism involves using the thoughts, ideas, or writings of another person and passing them off as your own. [5]
- Self-plagiarism is submitting the same piece of work for more than one course without the instructor's permission. [4]

Laurier university-wide:
- To request a deferred final exam on religious grounds, students submit the "Student Request for Accommodation for Religious Observances" form at least 7 calendar days before the final day of classes of the term. [5]
- For deferral requests on medical grounds, students can use a personal attestation, available on the petition form, in lieu of documentation, within the maximum of five deferred examinations permitted. [6]
- For unforeseen medical grounds, requests should be submitted as soon as possible and no later than three business days after the scheduled date of the examination. [6]
- If a conflict occurs, students can submit a Conflict Form at least 7 calendar days before the final day of classes of the term. [7]
- Requests after the deadline can be submitted as a deferred exam petition to the appropriate Petitions Committee, and if approved, the exam will be scheduled during the deferred exam period with a non-refundable deferred examination fee. [5][7]

- To appeal your final grade, you should first review the Grade Appeals information and then complete the Grade Appeal Request form, which is used to appeal your final grade in a course and includes regrading all of the course work done in the course. [7]
- The final grade appeal process addresses concerns regarding the application of grading criteria to the work submitted, and/or the calculation of grades only. [8]
- If you believe your submitted work was graded incorrectly during the term, you should follow the instructions on the syllabus for addressing such concerns, or promptly raise the issue with the instructor. [8]
- There are 4 sequential steps for a grade appeal, starting with the instructor. [8]
